punchline: Some of the work of remembering what you studied happens after you have closed the book.
thirty_sec: We think learning happens at the desk. The authors of Make It Stick say that's only the start. A new memory is fragile, and the brain keeps strengthening and reorganising it after you stop, with sleep seeming to help. Then, when you come back later and have to work to recall it, the memory gets stronger again. So a gap and a second try beat one more hour of repeating.
question: Have you ever crammed the night before something and found it had mostly vanished a few days later?
